Maintenance Report — MNT-0053-002

Asset: WELL-0053 (SW-24 Well 053, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 20 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 28 Feb 2023 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 943 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0053-0013 on 2023-01-19 Report written: 28 Feb 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0053-0013 showed the wellhead at 10.1 °C with the air at 7.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 37 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 254 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 203 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0053 (SW-24 Well 053, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 09 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Feb 2024 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 21 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0053-0068 at 10:15 on 2024-02-08 found crude oil on the pad: about 0.7% of the pad area, estimated 0.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0053-0111 showed the wellhead at 12.0 °C with the air at 12.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0053-0167 at 13:30 on 2026-01-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.0% of the pad area, estimated 1.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 254 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 203 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.4 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0053-029 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.88% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
  • Start a root-cause analysis for this equipment before the next repair is closed (well-type manual, section 10).
